newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends firmer on Cenbnk dlr sales.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends firmer on Cenbnk dlr sales.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed firmer on large dollar sales by the Central Bank, traders said, ending the session stronger at 492.25/493.25 per dollar despite large investor demand for foreign exchange.
The unit ended Thursday at 492.50/493.50 per dollar.
"The Central Bank came in hard ... selling maybe some $80 or $90 million today ... It sold to firm the exchange rate," said one trader.
Brokers said dollar demand had partly been fueled by low domestic interest rates as well as foreign selling on the Caracas stock exchange, which followed Brazil's plunging bourse down.
"I think the Bank will hold the bolivar at this level," said one trader.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.
